note:
wagmi takes 1.4.5. Two releases are crossed, 1.4.3 to 1.4.5, and 1.4.4 is
skipped. The apply writes 1.4.5's changelog entry and then back-fills 1.4.4's
below it, so this claw's own record carries both.

The releases: 1.4.4 and 1.4.5 are both class fix, disruption quiet. No core
floor moves in either. Codex stays at 0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the
same values 1.4.3 declared.

1.4.4 carries no landing section. Its errata paragraph says that every release
before it emptied the machine-wide skill directory of anything the release did
not carry, and that a firm who lost a skill that way has to put it back. This
claw lost nothing: its machine-wide directory held claw-ops alone before this
promotion, measured at 15:16Z, so there is nothing to restore.

The box, measured on wagmi-claw at 15:16Z before this note was written:
claw-members holds two people, jeremiah and abigail. Both have the
persistent-session core installed. It reads 2.1.252 for one and 2.1.227 for the
other, and both meet the floor. Both read codex 0.147.0. No member reads as
below a floor, so this claw's own classifier will not defer the release to the
quiet window. Both members' wake rails are running and both read adapter claude
in the ready state, taken as each member rather than as root.

A claw carrying its own skills in the machine-wide tier now passes its apply.
1.4.4 is the release that did not. It shipped the fix that keeps those skills,
and the sibling control in the same phase took its expected count from the
manifest while reading the tier, so the run failed on every claw that had such a
skill. From 1.4.5 that control reads the tier three times and passes on a delta
of one, whatever the tier already holds. Its line says how many entries the core
sees there that the release did not install, and says those are the claw's own.

The control has two arms no claw has exercised. One fires when a firm's entry
carries a name the manifest also declares. The other fires when the tier reads
short of what the release installed. Both are driven in the build repository's
own harness against fixture counts. Reaching either on a live claw means damage
to it, so they stay harness-proven.

The ride flag arrives with this apply and is not used by it. From 1.4.5 the
updater takes commonclaw-update.sh --release TAG, which rides a named release
from a channel at or below this claw's own. It refuses a tag no such channel
carries, and it refuses a run nobody is standing at. The updater this claw runs
today is 1.4.3's and has no such flag, so this promotion moves the pointer
first, the way every promotion before it did. The first ride from a tag is
1.5.0's business.

The line at the top of a ride names one channel once. On a first-tier claw it
says the claw's own pointer carried the tag. On a lower tier it names the
channel it read. Only the wording changed, and a ride resolves the same tag from
the same channel it did before.
